evidence.source: Shuowen.org, quoting the Shuowen Jiezi and Duan Yucai’s commentary
evidence.text: The Shuowen glosses 關 as a piece of wood laid crosswise to secure a doorway and analyzes it as 門 plus phonetic 𢇅. Duan Yucai lists later extensions including a border gate, closing, a mechanism, and a point of connection. This records historical dictionary assertions; it does not independently establish the dates or exact path of each extension.
evidence.title: 說文解字「關」 - Shuowen.org

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The entry repeats the Shuowen analysis and lists senses with textual examples: a door bar (citing the Han Shu), shut/close (Tao Yuanming, Eastern Jin), a frontier or mountain pass (citing Mencius and Jia Yi), a mechanism (Hou Hanshu), connection/concern (Song poetry), and other later senses. This supplies distinct cited uses, but the page does not date the composition of the cited passages or demonstrate every semantic link.
evidence.title: 關 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants, drawing on the Hanyu Guwenzi Xingbiao
evidence.text: The entry treats 関 and other shapes as variants of 關. Its note says a form in the bronze inscription called 關中布 resembles the modern variant 𨳹 and cautiously suggests it may be that variant’s source; it describes other variants as differing brush forms or clerical transformations. This does not establish a chronological ancestor relationship between 関 and simplified 关.
evidence.title: [A04398] 關 - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.source: Academia Sinica, Character Evolution Database
evidence.text: The database record for 關 identifies a bronze inscription entry (Jicheng 10371; Jinwen Gulin index 12.74) and a Small Seal form under Shuowen. The textual page does not display the glyphs or date the particular bronze inscription, so it supports the presence of catalogued bronze evidence but does not permit a visual assessment or precise first-attestation claim here.
evidence.title: 漢字「關」：字形演變

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The entry gives Mandarin pinyin guān. Among the senses it separately documents door-bar, shutting, frontier-pass, mechanism, connection, and involvement, with examples attributed to works from the Han through Qing periods. These citations show that dictionary ordering of glosses should not be treated as chronology.
evidence.title: 關 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: Baxter and Sagart, Old Chinese: A New Reconstruction, accessed through the book’s searchable PDF
evidence.text: The appendix lists 關 guān, Middle Chinese kwaen, Old Chinese *[k]ˤro[n], glossed ‘barrier’ (p. 214). The notation is Baxter–Sagart’s 2014 reconstruction system. This supports the character’s reconstructed pronunciation, not the pronunciation or name of any hypothesized depicted latch/object.
evidence.title: Old Chinese: A New Reconstruction

evidence.source: Wiktionary, Chinese readings and historical phonology citing Baxter–Sagart
evidence.text: The page gives Standard Mandarin guān (Pinyin), Standard Cantonese gwaan1 (Jyutping), and Baxter–Sagart values Middle Chinese ‹kwæn› and Old Chinese /*[k]ˁro[n]/ for 關. These are readings of 關 itself. They do not independently establish the sound value of a hypothesized original object depicted in a bronze graph.
evidence.title: 關 - Wiktionary

evidence.source: Princeton University, Startwords
evidence.text: The page reproduces the opening of the Classic of Poetry poem 關雎, including 關關雎鳩, and gives a comparative table for 關: Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese *kʕro[n], Middle Chinese kwaen, modern Mandarin guān. This is an early literary occurrence of the graph/word 關關, used in a bird-call expression; it is not evidence that this occurrence means ‘barrier’ or that the poem attests the barrier sense.
evidence.title: Of Sonorous Medieval Chinese Texts and NLP Model Training

evidence.source: Education Bureau, Hong Kong SAR, recommended passages PDF
evidence.text: The document prints the Classic of Poetry line ‘關關雎鳩，在河之洲’ and explains 關關 as the responding, harmonious sound of the birds. It dates the anthology broadly to songs from early Western Zhou (or earlier) through mid-Spring and Autumn, while characterizing this poem specifically as late Western Zhou. This is a dated literary use of the repeated expression, but the sound-to-barrier semantic connection is not established by this text.
evidence.title: 國風・關雎 詩經

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The dictionary lists 关 among variants of 關, while its entry explicitly describes 関 as a variant form. It does not say that modern simplified 关 descends from 関. Therefore the dossier’s claim that 关 was adapted from cursive 關 and its separate claim that it was simplified from 関 are not independently resolved by this source.
evidence.title: 關 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: Chinese Ministry of Education government portal, quoting the 1956 State Council resolution
evidence.text: The resolution states that the first batch of 230 simplified characters was to be used in printed and handwritten documents nationwide from 1 February 1956. The page establishes the standardization context and date; the retrieved text does not itself show the specific entry for 关 or explain its graphic derivation.
evidence.title: 国务院关于公布汉字简化方案的决议(1956年)

evidence.source: Japan National Diet Library Research Navi
evidence.text: The library notes that Japan adopted new standard forms through official character lists issued from 1946 to 1951. Separate official and variant-dictionary results identify 関 as a Japanese new form/variant of 關. This is a distinct Japanese standardization history and should not be conflated with the mainland Chinese 关 form.
evidence.title: 漢字表（字種・字体の変遷）を調べる

evidence.source: Shuowen.org, quoting Duan Yucai’s commentary on the Shuowen
evidence.text: The cited Shuowen analysis assigns 門 the semantic role and 𢇅 the phonetic role. The source does not provide an independent reconstruction for 𢇅 on this page, so the sound role is a historical lexicographic assertion rather than a fully checked sound comparison here. No whole-graph loan is required by this analysis.
evidence.title: 說文解字「關」 - Shuowen.org

evidence.source: Wiktionary, glyph-origin section for 關
evidence.text: One account describes an early bronze form as 門 plus 卝, interpreting 卝 as two wooden locking sticks and allowing that it might also have been phonetic; it then analyzes a later form as 門 plus phonetic 𢇅. This specific depiction and object interpretation is an attributed account, not confirmed by the text-accessible paleographic record inspected here. The proposed object’s original name and pronunciation were not independently recovered, so no borrowing claim based on that object’s name is established.
evidence.title: 關 - Wiktionary

evidence.source: CUHK 漢語多功能字庫 (Multi-function Chinese Character Database)
evidence.text: The entry displays two seal-script examples and eleven bronze-script examples for 關. Its analysis records competing accounts: bronze graphs are described as 門 plus 卝, with 卝 variously treated as a phonetic, a prototype of 關, or a depiction of two bars and a looped lock; it also records forms with 串, identified there as phonetic. The page cites the 鄂君啟舟節 for a bronze-period use meaning a frontier pass. These are the database’s reported analyses and attestations, not a resolution of the competing graphic readings.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.source: Academia Sinica, Xiaoxuetang
evidence.text: The official site describes its character-evolution database as covering oracle-bone, bronze, Warring States, seal and clerical-transition forms. The entry-specific query URL for 關 could not be accessed through the web tool, so no Xiaoxuetang form or label is selected here.
evidence.title: 小學堂

evidence.source: Academia Sinica, Xiaoxuetang
evidence.text: The official notice says glyph images and glyph-attribute information obtained through the site’s query interface are released under CC0 1.0. This applies to query-interface images and attributes, not to other linked content or other Academia Sinica sites.
evidence.title: 版權聲明

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The entry lists 关 and 関 among variants of 關. For 関 it quotes older lexicographic sources and classifies it as a variant, but this entry does not establish that simplified 关 descends from 関. It also records a cautious proposal that a form in the bronze inscription called 關中布 resembles, and may be the source of, 𨳹; that is a separate proposed relation.
evidence.title: [A04398] 關 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: CUHK 漢語多功能字庫, quoting 說文解字 and summarizing traditional analyses
evidence.text: The entry reproduces 說文’s analysis of 關 as 从門、𢇅聲 and defines it as wood laid crosswise to secure a doorway. This supports 門 as the stated semantic component and 𢇅 as the stated phonetic component in the seal-script analysis. The entry gives 關’s fanqie 古還切 and Middle Chinese rhyme-class information, but the inspected page does not provide a historical reconstruction for 𢇅 itself; a sound comparison between the two is therefore not established here.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.source: CUHK 漢語多功能字庫, quoting and discussing early textual examples
evidence.text: The database cites the 鄂君啟舟節 inscription for 關 meaning a frontier pass, and cites 《詩經・關雎》 for 關關 as a bird-call expression. It treats these as different textual uses; the page does not establish that the bird-call expression is the same lexical root as ‘barrier’ or establish a semantic path between the two. Its page gives no absolute date for the cited inscription.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.source: CUHK 漢語多功能字庫
evidence.text: The entry gives 關’s fanqie as 古還切 and Middle Chinese category information (initial 見, level tone, 山攝, 刪 rhyme, division 2, rounded). This is Middle Chinese rhyme-table classification rather than an Old Chinese reconstruction. No independently checked historical pronunciation for 𢇅 was found in the inspected pages; therefore no same-system reconstruction comparison is supplied.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫

search_audit.outcome: Inspected CUHK entry, Xiaoxuetang technical report and Shuowen.org page. CUHK page supplies labeled bronze and seal glyph links in its page description, but direct images return empty content in the web tool and the entry-specific Xiaoxuetang query URL was inaccessible.

gaps: The Academia Sinica text view records a bronze-inscription item for 關 but does not display a glyph or date the inscription; no glyph image was visually inspected. Earliest securely datable graphic attestation remains unresolved from accessed text.

The claim that the bronze form depicts two sticks locking a door is reported by Wiktionary, but its actual graphic evidence and interpretation could not be checked against a visible inscription image. The name/pronunciation of the hypothesized depicted object is unrecovered, so an object-name-based whole-graph phonetic loan is unsupported.

The phonetic component 𢇅 is identified by the Shuowen and attributed modern accounts, but its exact form-history and independent historical pronunciation comparison were not established by inspected source pages. The character’s own Baxter–Sagart readings are supplied; no matching reconstruction for 𢇅 was verified here.

關關 in the Classic of Poetry is an early literary bird-call expression, but whether this is a use of the same lexical root as ‘barrier’ or a distinct sound word/loan is unresolved. A pronoun-like or bird-call reconstruction alone cannot establish the depicted object’s name.

The semantic passage from crossbar/door fastener to shutting, frontier passes, mechanisms, involvement, and relation is supported by dictionary examples and commentary, but individual transitions are not all demonstrated by dated intermediate attestations in the inspected sources.

The textual record verified 1956 simplification standardization but did not establish the precise graphic source for 关 or prove derivation from 関. Treat the dossier’s competing simplification explanations as unresolved.

A contemporary Simplified Mandarin and Cantonese reading for 关 is not separately attested in the inspected external source; the listed readings directly concern 關, whose conventional simplified correspondence is 关.

The entry-specific Xiaoxuetang query for 關 was inaccessible through the web tool, so no exact Xiaoxuetang image URL or label could be verified. The general CC0 notice was inspected, but it does not license an unverified candidate image.

CUHK’s 關 entry reports eleven bronze-script and two seal-script glyph examples, but its linked direct image pages returned no readable contents. Since no direct image URL and provenance record could be verified from the inspected page output, no glyph image is proposed.

No image was visually inspected. The CUHK and Ministry records support candidate forms and textual descriptions only; they do not establish an image candidate’s pixel content or exact artifact identity.
The bronze analysis has competing explanations for 卝 and other components; the inspected page does not settle whether these forms depict a door lock, encode sound, or represent an earlier graph.
The proposed sound role of 𢇅 is supported here as a 說文 assertion. The inspected sources did not provide an independently checked historical pronunciation for 𢇅 to compare with 關.
The bronze-period pass attestation is cited by the CUHK database, but the page inspected does not date that specific inscription; a precise first-attestation date is unresolved.
The bird-call use 關關 and the barrier/door-bar uses remain lexically and semantically unconnected in the inspected sources. No object-name-based whole-graph loan is established.
